text:
maya: starting a quick investigation — running weight-only int8 (llm.int8 / bitsandbytes) on solstice13b to reproduce the p90 latency spike we saw in prod yesterday. batch=1, kv-cache enabled, decode length 1024.

samir: any perf logs yet? is this on Dedicated or Hosted?

maya: hosted (us-west). ETA for a first profile ~10m. command: ```python serve_bench.py --model solstice13b --quant llmint8 --backend bnb --batch 1 --max_len 1024 --kv_cache True --profile```

jen: fyi we recently flipped continuous-batching=on for that pool. could be coupling with int8 runtime.

maya: noted — I'll toggle continuous-batching off and re-run after the first baseline.

perf-bot: summary: run_id=r-1758502468, model=solstice13b, quant=llm.int8, p50=28ms, p90=420ms, p99=980ms, tokens/s=78. traces attached to r-1758502468 in perf-dashboard. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

samir: that p90 is terrible vs expected ~150ms. can you dump tail traces (heap, gpu-util, kernel times)?

maya: attaching quick snippet from nsys and dmesg tails: ```NSYS: avg kernel launch 0.9ms, aten::layer_norm 12ms, attention_mm 200ms (spiky). GPU util 42-98% (spiky), cuda_memcpy 8ms spikes. dmesg: no OOMs, some nvlink re-negotiation logs at 02:14:03.```

alex: is this only on long context? we saw attention_mm blow up when kv-cache misses cause recompute for attention with past state.

maya: repro is with 1024 decode; I ran same prompt with max_len=128 -> p90=160ms, p99=280ms. big delta when length expands.

jen: hypothesis: weight-only int8 has a codepath that switches kernel tiling based on sequence length; with continuous-batching and long sequences it picks a different GEMM kernel that's slower on this HW.

samir: actionable tests: (1) run with continuous-batching off (maya doing), (2) run with bnb 4bit fallback (force fp16 for attention matmul), (3) try pinned allocator and smaller batch.

maya: ran (1): continuous-batching off -> p90 180ms, p99 320ms. improvement.

perf-bot: updated summary for run r-1758502672 (cont-batch=off): p50=26ms, p90=178ms, p99=318ms, tokens/s=74.

maya: ran (2): forced attention ops in fp16 via env WARN_FORCE_FP16_ATTENTION=1 -> p90 170ms, p99 300ms, but token quality seems identical on quick sample. will run eval slice overnight.

samir: interesting. so it's a kernel-selection/tiling perf cliff interacting with batching. ops: can we add a routing rule to prefer fp16-attn fallback for requests >512 tokens until we fix llm.int8 kernels? low-risk and documented.

ops_bot: ticket created: INF-1109 "int8 weight-only attention kernel p90 spike for long-context" assigned eng-runtime, priority P2. linked runs: r-1758502468, r-1758502672.

jen: also add a canary with quantized model but with kv_cache disabled to collect quality deltas (some tasks rely on past tokens).

alex: for deploy profile doc — recommend default policy: if request_length > 512 then route to model_variant(fp16-attn) else use llm.int8. add flag in model config: `long_context_fallback: true`.

maya: noted. I'll patch the model config in staging and run an eval comparing the two routes (LLM.INT8 vs FP16-attn fallback) on our 10k long-context slice. will post results in the ticket.

samir: thanks — prioritize slice that hit prod errors. if eval shows <0.5% accuracy delta, we can push routing rule to hosted pools.

maya: quick note — quant-quality smoke looked fine on short prompts; it's the performance cliff with long contexts that's the operational risk. keeping this thread as the experiment log.

jen: thanks everyone. next check-in in ~12h after overnight eval. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
